query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a tailored thermomechanical treatment to reduce internal stresses in eutectic high-entropy alloys will improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility by relieving residual stresses and modifying the microstructure.
generation.material_initial_state: Dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries
generation.intervention: Tailored thermomechanical treatment with a temperature range of 500-700°C and a strain rate of 10^-4 s^-1
generation.structural_mediator: Internal stress reduction and microstructural modification
generation.mechanism: Relief of residual stresses and modification of the microstructure, leading to reduced microcracking and improved ductility
generation.predicted_outcome: 20% increase in strength and 30% increase in tensile ductility relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline
generation.boundary: Temperature range of 500-700°C and strain rate of 10^-4 s^-1
generation.uncertainty: The exact temperature and strain rate ranges may need to be optimized for specific alloy compositions, and the treatment may not be effective for all types of eutectic high-entropy alloys

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing of thermomechanically treated and untreated samples at room temperature
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the treated samples show less than 10% increase in strength or less than 20% increase in tensile ductility compared to the untreated samples, the hypothesis is falsified
